answer: A durable defense is a reputation thread that only grows through verified work over time. Each thread records completed tasks, peer attestations, and dispute outcomes, and high-value work needs a long, unbroken thread, so a fresh identity starts at the bottom of the canyon with no standing. An attacker can spawn a plume of new accounts, but each one must still climb the same slow slope: weeks of real work before it can touch valuable jobs. Faking that history costs more in compute and time than the rewards it could steal, and one detected fraud snaps the thread and burns the investment.
